Place two opposite scalar charges at separation r on the 3D lattice. Compute the total "energy" (action integrated over paths connecting the charges) as a function of r. origin/main:docs/ai_methodology/raw/prompts_session_04c820e1.md:1583:Nielsen-Ninomiya says that on a lattice with locality, hermiticity, and translational invariance, chiral fermion species must come in pairs with opposite chirality — the total chiral charge is zero. The deep reason is topological: the dispersion relation is a map from T^3 to the energy surface, and the zeros are constrained by the Poincare-Hopf theorem. The attack is to show that when Cl(3) is the on-site algebra, the Nielsen-Ninomiya counting is refined: the 8 corners of the Brillouin zone (the standard staggered doublers) organize into exactly 3 irreducible orbits under the Z_3 that is forced by Cl(3), and this Z_3 orbit structure is itself topologically protected. The key step is proving that the topological index that enforces doubling also enforces the specific 1+3+3+1 orbit decomposition, and that the three 3-fold sectors each carry a distinct Berry phase or winding number. This directly turns the "bug" of doubling into the "feature" of generations.
